comparison: Perfect agreement on apparatus design and technical specifications (C27-C34). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes documentation with Figure 1 and Table 1, while peer reviewers commend the detailed write-up for reproducibility.

Perfect agreement on overall contribution (C75, C91). Both evaluations support these high-level summary claims. OpenEval views them as appropriate synthesis of demonstrated capabilities, while peer reviewers describe the work as 'valuable' with 'clear and convincing advantages.'

Strong agreement on marmoset model rationale and background literature (C1, C7-C10, C12-C15). Both evaluations support these claims as well-established knowledge. OpenEval notes appropriate citations, while peer reviewers accept marmosets as 'a great platform to study primate social cognition.'

Strong agreement on video analysis methods (C43-C47). Both evaluations support the technical implementation. OpenEval emphasizes specific training parameters and citations, while peer reviewers confirm the paradigm allows 'precisely quantifying visual behavior' without challenging technical details.

Agreement on traditional method limitations (C22-C25). Both evaluations support these claims as appropriate motivation. OpenEval notes the characterization is well-cited but somewhat overstated, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these limitations as justification for the new apparatus.

Agreement on subject and housing details (C35-C39). Both evaluations support these methodological claims. OpenEval confirms adequate documentation of sample size and ethical approvals, while peer reviewers accept the training protocol and animal welfare procedures without challenge.

Agreement on high-throughput capability (C56, C58, C78). Both evaluations support the trial throughput data. OpenEval notes the calculation is mathematically correct but flags potential confounds in cross-species comparison, while peer reviewers unanimously affirm this as a major strength without questioning the data.

Divergence on learning speed claims (C54, C55). OpenEval supports these claims based on quantitative behavioral data, while peer reviewers express uncertainty—the editor explicitly states 'claims of faster social learning...will require further corroboration.'

Partial overlap on behavioral proficiency (C56, C57). OpenEval supports these claims with appropriate statistical reporting and justified proficiency criteria. Peer reviewers support the high-throughput aspect but do not separately evaluate the proficiency criterion claims.

Agreement on flexibility and parameter adjustability (C59-C62, C84). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes qualitative observations are reasonable despite lacking quantitative comparisons, while peer reviewers affirm the device 'allows for quantitative control and adjustment' as a demonstrated capability.

Agreement on neural recording integration (C71-C74, C89-C90). Both evaluations support the proof-of-concept demonstration. OpenEval notes limitations (n=1 animal, no statistical analysis), while peer reviewers affirm feasibility without challenge, noting 'the advantage of collecting neural and freely-behaving behavioral data concurrently.'

Agreement on neural recording methodology (C48-C52). Both evaluations support the technical methods. OpenEval confirms appropriate surgical procedures and spike sorting, while peer reviewers accept these as standard methodology without challenge.

Agreement on design flexibility and modularity (C3-C4, C63-C64, C85-C86). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes capabilities are demonstrated through construction and parameter manipulations but flags speculative applications, while peer reviewers consistently affirm flexibility as a strength.

Divergence on fine-grained behavioral analysis (C68). OpenEval rates as uncertain due to missing statistical details and n=1 animal limitation. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty—the editor states 'claims of finer-grained behavioural analysis...will require further corroboration.'

Divergence on temporal resolution claims (C65-C66). OpenEval supports these claims based on Figure 2B demonstration. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with the editor calling for 'further corroboration' of fine-grained behavioral analysis claims.

OpenEval evaluates limitations and success rate calculations (C80-C81) as supported and appropriately acknowledged. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these limitation claims.

OpenEval rates cross-species applicability claims (C87-C88) as uncertain, noting they are speculative without empirical validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these future application claims.

Peer reviewers support experimental methods and training protocol details (C40-C42) not separately evaluated by OpenEval. These claims are accepted without challenge as meeting methodological standards.
